theme: 3 terms on key paths: a value that points to a property, one that can also change it, and dot access through a subscript

terms.definition: A value that points to a property of a type, so you can read that property later.
terms.example: Pass the KeyPath `\.title` to `map`, and you get every song title.

terms.definition: A key path that can also change the property it points to on a mutable value.
terms.example: It's a WritableKeyPath, so the form can update any field.

terms.definition: An attribute that lets a type answer dot-style member access through one subscript you write.
terms.example: With Dynamic Member Lookup, `Box` shows the pet's `name` directly.

Learn to explain key paths in Swift: KeyPath, WritableKeyPath & Dynamic Member Lookup, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
KeyPath - A value that points to a property of a type, so you can read that property later.
WritableKeyPath - A key path that can also change the property it points to on a mutable value.
Dynamic Member Lookup - An attribute that lets a type answer dot-style member access through one subscript you write.

landscape.title: Swift KeyPath, WritableKeyPath & Dynamic Member Lookup | Day 43
landscape.description:
Explain KeyPath, WritableKeyPath & Dynamic Member Lookup in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
KeyPath, WritableKeyPath, 다이내믹 멤버 룩업 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

KeyPath - A value that points to a property of a type, so you can read that property later.
한국어: KeyPath: 타입의 프로퍼티를 가리켜서 나중에 그 프로퍼티를 읽을 수 있게 해 주는 값

WritableKeyPath - A key path that can also change the property it points to on a mutable value.
한국어: WritableKeyPath: 변경 가능한 값에서 가리키는 프로퍼티를 바꿀 수도 있는 키 패스

Dynamic Member Lookup - An attribute that lets a type answer dot-style member access through one subscript you write.
한국어: 다이내믹 멤버 룩업: 직접 만든 서브스크립트 하나로 점(.) 문법 멤버 접근에 답하게 해 주는 속성

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out how a type answers a property it does not have, what a key path points to and why setting failed, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain key paths in English?

dialogue.title: Where does title come from?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, `Track` has no `title` property, but `Track().title` compiles. How?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It uses Dynamic Member Lookup. Look at the attribute on top.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Swift turns `.title` into a KeyPath and passes it in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the KeyPath points to `title` inside `Song`?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. The subscript reads `song` at that path.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why can't I set `title` the same way?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because a KeyPath can only read. To write, you need a WritableKeyPath.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So I change the subscript to take a WritableKeyPath?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, and add a setter. Then Dynamic Member Lookup works both ways.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. KeyPath to read, WritableKeyPath to write, Dynamic Member Lookup for the dot.
A KeyPath points to a property without reading it yet.
